outcomes: An application declares a document collection once and receives typed identifiers, stored documents, filters, and repositories from that declaration
The memory and Firestore adapters implement the same portable repository contract and reject capabilities they cannot honor
A transaction either commits every write in one named store or exposes none of them
Operators can provision, observe, and close document backends without exposing credential values
nonGoals: Relational joins, SQL migrations, blobs, full-text search, aggregations, realtime listeners, or a backend-native query DSL
Transactions spanning more than one named document store
Promising identical optional capabilities for every adapter or parity with a document package in another language
Promising compatibility across every pre-1.0 minor release

requirements.text: Collection(), Field(), and DocumentId() produce one typed definition whose storage field mapping and full or partial validation are applied at the repository boundary.
save() replaces by default, merge writes are explicit, and save() or saveMany() returns the stored value read back from the adapter rather than echoing the caller's mutable input.
Repositories accept only the documented structured filter and order vocabulary, append document-id fields as deterministic ordering tie-breakers, and page through opaque cursors rather than offsets.
A zero result limit means zero rows, adapter bulk operations chunk their work, and deleteMany rejects an empty or entirely undefined filter instead of turning it into an unbounded delete.

An adapter implements the shared contract and rejects unsupported capabilities with typed document errors; Firestore therefore rejects composite identifiers and incompatible negative-filter combinations instead of approximating them.
runInTransaction() provides read-your-writes and atomic commit or rollback within one named store, and rejects access to a second store before it can partially participate.
A configured named store reuses one managed backend, different store names remain isolated, closeBackend() permits clean recreation, and the document plugin closes every managed backend at shutdown.
Firestore credentials accept inline JSON or a key-file path, malformed inline credentials raise a typed DocumentError, and no error includes the credential value.

Build-time infrastructure discovery groups Firestore collections by sorted named store, omits memory stores, de-duplicates collection names, and matches the shared document requirement fixture byte-for-byte.
Repository, backend lifecycle, and transaction outcomes emit collection-scoped duration, failure, slow-operation, and active-transaction measurements while remaining safe when telemetry is disabled.
